consensus_summary: Consensus presents no single settled primary but two dominant, widely attested streams: (1) the believer as pilgrim/sojourner/exile on earth whose true citizenship is heaven, and (2) the outsider/alien (ger/xenos) to covenant or community—often the vulnerable to whom hospitality is due and in whom Christ is met (Mt 25)—plus the related sense of Gentiles formerly strangers to the covenants now brought near (Eph 2). Negative or Christ-as-unrecognized-stranger readings are secondary.
book_summary: A non-citizen of God's commonwealth—one outside the covenant, drawn in, or, once in, made a stranger to the world (opposite: Knowing).
consensus_core_identification: Either the covenant/community outsider (to be welcomed or incorporated) or the believer as temporary sojourner whose home is not the present world.
book_core_identification: Non-citizen of God's commonwealth: the one outside the covenant who may be drawn in, or the one already in who is thereby made stranger to the world.
boundary_disagreement: Book centers solely on commonwealth/covenant citizenship status (outside drawn in, or inside vs. world) and omits the consensus's frequent hospitality/Mt 25 'Christ encountered in the vulnerable stranger' and negative (false voice/strange woman) extensions as definitional.
material_contradiction: None; the two statuses the book names are both standard consensus referents, merely unified and bounded under 'non-citizen of God's commonwealth' without denying other uses.
rationale: Minimum cores overlap on the Eph 2 alien-to-covenant and the pilgrim-to-world senses that dominate the blind responses. The book preserves those referents but refines by (a) subordinating them to a single commonwealth-citizenship frame, (b) making the dual 'outside-drawn-in / inside-stranger-to-world' the entire definition, and (c) excluding the hospitality-Christ and negative cases that several consensus responses treat as primary or common. This is boundary/precision revision, not replacement of the central category, hence REFINED rather than MATCH or DIVERGENT.
strongest_objection: Eph 2:12, 19 (the sole printed citations) explicitly move people from 'strangers' to 'no more strangers' inside the commonwealth, so they directly underwrite only the 'outside, drawn in' half; the 'once in, made a stranger to the world' half lacks printed support and must be inferred from uncited pilgrim texts.
